title: Estate planning: trusts, GRATs, dynasty planning
summary: For owners with substantial estates approaching the federal exemption ($15M individual / $30M couple in 2026), advanced planning preserves wealth across generations.
detailsHtml:
The federal estate tax — updated for 2026

Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 2025), the federal estate and gift tax exemption was permanently increased to $15M per individual ($30M per couple) effective January 1, 2026, indexed for inflation thereafter. This replaced the prior scheduled TCJA sunset that would have reverted the exemption to ~$7M. The marginal rate above the exemption remains 40%. Owners with estates approaching or projected to approach the exemption still benefit from advanced techniques, particularly given the meaningful state-level estate taxes in many jurisdictions (NY, MA, OR, WA, IL, MD, and others) with much lower thresholds than the federal exemption.

Key vehicles

GRATs (Grantor Retained Annuity Trusts): Transfer appreciating assets out of the estate with minimal gift tax. Effective when interest rates are low and assets are expected to appreciate substantially.

SLATs (Spousal Lifetime Access Trusts): One spouse gifts assets to an irrevocable trust benefiting the other spouse. Uses exemption while keeping family access to the assets indirectly.

Dynasty trusts (in favorable states like SD, NV, DE): Multi-generational trusts that hold assets outside the estate of each beneficiary, potentially for centuries.

None of this should be attempted without a qualified estate planning attorney. The complexity is significant; the cost of getting it wrong is significant. (For finding the attorney or financial-planning support, apply the fiduciary-vs-suitability filter on the Welcome view — estate attorneys generally operate under fiduciary duty to the client, but coordinating financial-planning teams often include suitability-standard professionals; surfacing the question early prevents the conflicted-recommendation pattern.)
